findings.description: The EC2 user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone with access to the instance (including via SSRF), and the credentials are stored unencrypted in the launch configuration and Terraform state.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device encryption settings are specified, so the instance's root volume may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with credentials in user data, an SSRF against the web server can trivially read the metadata and user-data endpoints.

The instance is launched into web_subnet, which is associated with a route table containing an internet gateway route, and the file outputs ec2_public_dns, indicating the host is directly internet-reachable while serving unauthenticated HTTP (apache2 over port 80, cleartext).
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data stored on the volume attached to the web host is unencrypted at rest.

The EBS snapshot is created from the volume without encryption enabled (the source volume is not encrypted, so the snapshot inherits an unencrypted state). Snapshot data, including any sensitive contents of the attached volume, is stored in cleartext and can be exposed if the snapshot is shared or its access controls fail.

The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the attached EC2 instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against the administrative interface.
Inbound TCP/80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unencrypted HTTP traffic from any source; any credentials or data served over this listener are transmitted in cleartext.

The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, which provides no outbound segmentation and facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control callbacks if the instance is compromised.

The subnet sets map_public_ip_on_launch = true, so every instance launched into it (including aws_instance.web_host) automatically receives a public IPv4 address and becomes directly reachable from the internet, removing the network boundary that would otherwise front the workload.
The subnet sets map_public_ip_on_launch = true, automatically exposing any instance or ENI launched into it to the public internet rather than requiring an explicit, deliberate public IP assignment.

The VPC is created without an accompanying aws_default_security_group resource restricting the default security group's rules. Resources launched without an explicit security group inherit the default group, which permits all traffic between its members and unrestricted egress.

The route table shared by both subnets sends all traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to the internet gateway, making every subnet associated with it a public subnet. Combined with the route table associations for web_subnet and web_subnet2, any instance or ENI placed there is directly reachable from and able to reach the internet, removing the private-subnet network boundary.

The second subnet is attached to the same route table that carries a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, so there is no private tier in the VPC; all workloads share a single publicly routed segment with no segmentation between tiers.
The S3 bucket that stores VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (no SSE-S3/KMS), so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted at rest.

No public access block or ACL/bucket policy restrictions are declared for the flow log bucket, relying entirely on account defaults; flow log data could become publicly readable if a permissive ACL or policy is later applied.
The bucket holding VPC flow logs has no server access logging configured, so unauthorized access to the security log data would leave no audit trail.

Versioning is not enabled on the flow log bucket, so log objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, undermining the integrity of security audit data. Combined with force_destroy = true, the entire log bucket and its contents can be deleted by a terraform destroy without safeguards.
No bucket policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests is attached, allowing flow log data to be retrieved over cleartext HTTP.
